findings.claim: (3) resolveField (the prefill/narrower-wins resolver): src/lib/profile/profileData.ts:259-271, exact code — `export function resolveField(ps: MyProfile[], field: 'name'|'email'): FieldResolution { const withValue = ps.filter(p=>p[field]!=='').slice().sort((a,b)=>NARROWNESS[a._sharing]-NARROWNESS[b._sharing]); return { value: withValue.length>0 ? withValue[0][field] : '', holders: withValue.map(p=>({level:p._sharing,id:p._id})) }; }` with `NARROWNESS = {private:0, domain:1, public:2}` (line 235) — i.e. rendered value = the value held by the entity at the MOST RESTRICTIVE (narrowest) non-empty sharing tier; `holders.length>1` signals a same-field cross-tier duplicate (an interrupted-move anomaly), returned rather than silently collapsed.
findings.evidence: Read profileData.ts 223-271 in full.

findings.claim: (3) The up-to-three-profile shape: `MyProfile { _id: string; name: string; email: string; _sharing: Level }` (profileData.ts:123-128), `Level = 'public'|'domain'|'private'` (line 120), read via `listMyProfiles` which GETs `entity?_type.string=profile&_parent.reference={personId}&props=name,email,_sharing&limit=10` — profiles are children of the person entity, 'a member has up to three profile entities' (one per level), limit=10 is an explicit ample bound, and an unknown `_sharing` value throws rather than silently defaulting.
findings.evidence: Read profileData.ts 119-204 in full.

findings.claim: (3) Roster does NOT use resolveField for the row's NAME — deliberately. `toRosterRow` (rosterData.ts:214-238) inlines its own domain-or-public scan for `name` (never private, domain preferred over public when both exist) specifically because `resolveField` sorts private FIRST and would leak a private-only name (contradicting a #28/#58 ruling). `email`, by contrast, IS rendered via `resolveField(profiles,'email').value` (line 231) as-is, because roster-context profiles can never legitimately carry a private email for that resolver to wrongly prefer. So resolveField is the prefill/resolution mechanism for #268's EMAIL field but is explicitly the WRONG tool for a NAME field if 'never leak private' matters the same way here — worth flagging since #268's contract says email prefill uses 'the roster's existing resolveField narrower-wins' but says nothing about reusing it for name (name prefill per #268 is a one-time COPY from the person's profile display name, a different, ADJACENT mechanism, not the roster's own inline domain-or-public scan, and not resolveField either).
findings.evidence: Read rosterData.ts 193-238 in full (doc comment + code).

findings.claim: (4) admin_member_record provisioned def, exact quote (scripts/migrations/lib/mvox-schema-extensions.ts:211-286): `sharing:'domain'`, `inheritsRights:true`, one required parent (`database`, card 1/0..N). Properties: `person` (reference, required, sharing:'domain', ordinal 1); `name` (string, required, sharing:'domain', ordinal 2, table:true); `phone` (string, optional, sharing:'private', ordinal 3); `email` (string, optional, sharing:'private', ordinal 4); `birthdate` (type:'datetime', optional, sharing:'private') with the note: 'stored as a full datetime (no distinct date-only wire type observed elsewhere in this schema) — UI renders the date portion only'. Design notes (lines 278-284) pin: ONE record per person is an app-level invariant (check-then-create, Entu has no native uniqueness constraint); instance `_sharing` asserted explicitly as `domain` at create time (not inherited); R4 prefill is a ONE-TIME plain-value copy at create, never a formula/live reference; commissioned by mvox-app#265.
findings.evidence: Read scripts/migrations/lib/mvox-schema-extensions.ts:211-286 in full.

findings.claim: (4) Per-property `sharing` on a PropertySpec (name/phone/email each carrying their own domain/private tier within the SAME entity type) is a SCHEMA/prop-def-level bucket ('gate 1 of the 3-gate-AND bucket model', PropertySpec.sharing doc, lines 40-76) — already provisioned once at migration time, NOT something the per-instance CREATE payload repeats. The per-INSTANCE write only ever sends ONE `_sharing` value (entity-level, e.g. `{type:'_sharing', string:'domain'}`) alongside `_type`/`_parent`/`_inheritrights` — confirmed by every live create body in the codebase (createProfile: `{type:'_type',reference:...},{type:'_parent',...},{type:'_inheritrights',boolean:false},{type:'_sharing',string:input._sharing}`, profileData.ts:84-93; createSection sends `_sharing:'public'` the same way, sectionActions.ts:50). So #268's 'explicit _sharing per property AND on the record' most likely means: the four field-level tiers are the ALREADY-PROVISIONED prop-def buckets quoted above (nothing new to send per property at write time), plus the record's OWN entity `_sharing:'domain'` asserted explicitly in the create POST (never omitted/inherited) — this reading is grounded in the def's own design note but the actual admin_member_record CREATE code does not exist yet, so how #268 will literally structure the array is [speculative] beyond this precedent.
findings.evidence: Read PropertySpec doc (mvox-schema-extensions.ts:40-76) and two live create bodies (profileData.ts:84-93, sectionActions.ts full read 1-140).

findings.claim: (4) UPDATE path precedent: `replaceEntityProperty(cfg, entityId, value, fetchImpl, label)` (src/lib/entu/replaceProperty.ts:64-106) is the ONE post-#264 atomic single-property overwrite: GET `entity/{id}?props={prop}` for existing value id(s) → POST `entity/{id}` body `[{_id:<first existing id>, ...value}]` (or bare `[value]` if none existed) in one call (Entu's native overwrite: a POST value entry carrying an existing value's `_id` soft-deletes that old value in the SAME call) → any EXTRA stale ids (corrupted multi-value only) get individually DELETEd strictly after the POST lands. Non-2xx anywhere throws; the module's own header explicitly documents this is NOT compare-and-swap (a double-fire race can still duplicate a value — callers must single-flight-guard). Four live callers already reuse it as-is: eventFieldEdit.ts:45, repertoireActions.ts (status:100, edition-pin:114, position:182). A #268 field-by-field save (name/phone/email/birthdate) on an EXISTING admin_member_record would call this once per changed field.
findings.evidence: Read replaceProperty.ts in full (109 lines); grepped its 4 call sites.

findings.claim: (4) CREATE payload conventions, quoted verbatim from the closest live analogue (createProfile, profileData.ts:60-109): props array is `[{type:'_type',reference:profileTypeId},{type:'_parent',reference:input.personId},{type:'_inheritrights',boolean:false},{type:'_sharing',string:input._sharing}, ...ownerIds.map(id=>({type:'_owner',reference:id}))]`, POSTed to `entity` (not `entity/{id}` — plain create), response `_id` required or throws ('apparent-success trap'). `_type` is always a resolved REFERENCE via `resolveTypeId(cfg, typeName)` (entuSeasons.ts:26-46), never a literal string (sectionActions.ts:34-35 pins this explicitly as a #10 finding). By direct analogy, an admin_member_record create would resolve `resolveTypeId(cfg,'admin_member_record')`, `_parent`=the database entity id (same attachment point as `member`, per the schema def's own parent note), `_inheritrights:true` (boolean — matches `inheritsRights:true` in the def, unlike profile's `false`), `_sharing:'domain'` (string), `person:{reference:personId}`, `name:{string:...}`, optional `phone`/`email` as `{string:...}`, optional `birthdate` as `{datetime:<ISO string>}`. This exact array has NOT been written anywhere yet — [speculative] synthesis from verified sibling patterns, not a quoted existing function.
findings.evidence: Read profileData.ts:60-109 and entuSeasons.ts resolveTypeId (26-46) and sectionActions.ts's own #264-item-6 `_inheritrights:true` rationale (61-68).

findings.claim: (5) Date-only render-without-day-shift tooling: `isoDateFormatter(timeZone?)` (src/lib/preferences/timeFormat.ts:151-162) is the shared en-CA `YYYY-MM-DD` Intl.DateTimeFormat factory (#231 GREEN, replacing 7 duplicate constructions). The proven anti-day-shift pattern is `isoDateFormatter('UTC').format(new Date(isoString))` — used identically at three sites: season bounds (`+page.svelte:2707,2714-2719`, `seasonDateFmt = isoDateFormatter('UTC')`, guarded against `Invalid Date` throwing), library lending dates (`routes/library/+page.svelte:45,57-61`, comment: 'Entu delivers full ISO timestamps... Forces UTC timezone so date-only values never shift to the previous day in negative offsets'), and agenda/event date-key formatters (AgendaList.svelte, AgendaMonthView.svelte, both `isoDateFormatter(TZ)`). This same call (`isoDateFormatter('UTC').format(new Date(record.birthdate))`, `.slice` not needed since the formatter already yields exactly `YYYY-MM-DD`) is the direct, already-proven technique for #268's date-only render of a `datetime`-typed birthdate.
findings.evidence: Read timeFormat.ts:140-167; read +page.svelte:2696-2719; read library/+page.svelte:44-61; grepped all isoDateFormatter call sites.

findings.claim: (5) Native `<input type=date>` round-trip precedent for a value that IS already date-only on the wire: season start/end dates are stored via Entu's `date`-typed property slot (wire key `date`, not `datetime` — `entityCreate.ts:447-448: {type:'start_date',date:start},{type:'end_date',date:end}`; read back via `entuSeasons.ts:98-99: raw.start_date?.[0]?.date?.slice(0,10)`) and bound to the native date input's `value` completely RAW (`seasonManageStartDate = season?.startDate ?? ''` at `+page.svelte:2857`, and the input's `value={seasonManageStartDate}` elsewhere) — NO Date object round-trip at all for editing, because the stored string is already `YYYY-MM-DD`-compatible (Entu normalizes `date` values to midnight-UTC ISO timestamps on read, and the app just `.slice(0,10)`s them). This is DIFFERENT from what #268 needs: admin_member_record.birthdate is typed `datetime` (see finding above), not Entu's `date` slot, so there is NO existing call site anywhere that converts a native date-input's `YYYY-MM-DD` value INTO a `datetime`-typed wire value — the schema def's own note ('no distinct date-only wire type observed elsewhere in THIS schema') flags this as new ground. The anti-shift technique to reuse is the same UTC-anchoring principle (build the write as UTC midnight, e.g. `` `${dateStr}T00:00:00.000Z` ``, and always format/parse that string with `isoDateFormatter('UTC')`), but the WRITE side of this exact conversion is [speculative] — nothing in the repo does it yet.
findings.evidence: Read entuSeasons.ts:85-105, entityCreate.ts wire-shape comments (65-79, 442-479), +page.svelte:2853-2858 (season fields seeded from raw startDate/endDate string), and cross-checked with grep for 'T00:00:00'/'toISOString()' across src (no date-input→datetime-property write precedent found).

findings.claim: (6) #245/#157 pencil precedent (event-detail page): EVERY editable header field (name, event_type, start_datetime, duration_minutes, location, description) uses the SAME whole-field-button idiom — a `<button>` (never a bare glyph or a div+role) spanning the WHOLE field's tap target (`min-h-11 w-full`, `appearance-none`), containing an sr-only `<span>` label as its FIRST child followed by the visible value span(s), so the accessible name COMPOSES from contents ('Edit event name, Tuesday Rehearsal') rather than being silenced by an `aria-label` (which would override descendant content). Exact quote, event/[id]/+page.svelte:2334-2351 (`name` field) and :2253-2263 (`event_type`, #245's own comment explicitly calling it 'the SIXTH #157 whole-field activator').
findings.evidence: Read event/[id]/+page.svelte:2295-2360 and 2218-2264 in full, including the inline design-rationale comments.

findings.claim: (6) #262 per-row a11y-name lesson (event-schedule rows, same file): the per-row edit button's accessible name is built the SAME way — a STATIC, generic sr-only label (`m.event_schedule_edit_aria_label()`, not templated per-row) as a CHILD of the button, immediately followed by the row's own visible `event-schedule-row-name`/`event-schedule-row-time` spans INSIDE the same button — so the composed name is 'Edit schedule item, {name}, {time}' for FREE via name-from-contents, without ever templating the row's identity into an aria-label string. The review comment (lines 2765-2771) explicitly diagnoses the alternative as broken: an `aria-label` on the wrapper 'overrides descendant content, so the row announced "Edit kogunemine" and swallowed the TIME'. This is the exact mechanism #268's `roster-row-record-edit-{memberId}` accessible name should reuse: sr-only generic label + visible member-name span, both inside the pencil button, never a templated aria-label.
findings.evidence: Read event/[id]/+page.svelte:2759-2796 in full including the #262 review comments.

findings.claim: (6) The roster page currently has NO per-member-row button at all that could anchor this pattern by copy-paste — the only existing per-row interactive elements in `memberRow` are the SectionPicker trigger (a labelled trigger button, `section-picker-trigger-{memberId}`, inside SectionPicker.svelte) and the deactivate/reinstate buttons (plain visible-text buttons, `member-deactivate-{memberId}`/`member-reinstate-{memberId}`, no sr-only composition needed since their own visible label already names the action, not per-member identity). Neither currently follows the #157/#262 sr-only-child-composes-with-visible-content idiom, because neither needs to (their visible text alone is sufficient) — #268's pencil is the FIRST roster-row control that needs it, since a bare pencil glyph carries no name of its own.
findings.evidence: Read memberRow snippet in full (2671-2803) and grepped SectionPicker.svelte testids.

risks: No admin_member_record data-layer code exists anywhere in the repo yet (grep confirms only the schema-extensions.ts definition) — every CREATE/read/check-then-create wire shape in this report beyond the def itself is synthesized by analogy to sibling create/read functions, not read from an implemented call site. Flag clearly to whoever builds #268: the analogy is strong (same _type/_parent/_sharing/_inheritrights vocabulary, same person.reference query shape) but unverified against a real endpoint response.

Which sr-only role=status region #268 should target is unresolved by the codebase: there are four existing SECTION-scoped regions (reorder/remove/create/rename) and zero member-row-action regions; deactivate/reinstate currently announce nothing via a live region. #268 will most likely need a FIFTH new region following the identical idiom, but nothing pins its testid or var name — needs a design decision, not just a mapping.

Writing a native <input type=date> value into a datetime-typed property (birthdate) with zero day-shift has no existing call site to copy: season/library date fields are Entu 'date'-slot values (already date-only on read), never converted from a date-input into a 'datetime' wire value. The UTC-midnight-anchor technique is well-established for RENDER (isoDateFormatter('UTC')) but the WRITE-side conversion function does not exist yet and must be built + tested fresh, including its round-trip against whatever exact ISO string Entu's own datetime property normalizes to.

toRosterRow's name resolution deliberately avoids resolveField to prevent a private-tier leak (rosterData.ts:197-202); #268's contract text says email prefill reuses 'resolveField narrower-wins' but is silent on whether NAME prefill should mirror the roster's own inline domain-or-public scan, use resolveField directly (risking the same leak class rosterData.ts explicitly rejected), or do something else — worth a scope-check before implementation rather than assuming resolveField covers both fields identically.

The check-then-create read's exact limit/detection threshold for '>1 = damaged data' is unverified against any live admin_member_record data (none exists) — the two cited person.reference precedents use limit=50 (multi-collective) and limit=1+status filter (uniqueness-by-filter), neither of which is quite the 'small N to catch duplicates directly' shape #268 needs; this number needs an explicit decision, not just inheritance from precedent.

findings.claim: (4) The standing write-layer convention across profileData.ts/applyProfileSave.ts throws Error/*SaveError objects whose messages are STATIC step+status strings (e.g. 'saveProfileFields save failed: 500', 'profile field save failed after create') — never interpolated field values (name/email). The one existing typed partial-failure class, SectionReparentPartialError, likewise carries only step/counts/HTTP status/RESPONSE body text — never the outgoing request payload. Existing console.error call sites on roster write paths (deactivate/reinstate) log only a context string + memberId + the error object, never field values. No PII-in-logs bug exists today because nothing PII-shaped is written yet; the finding is that the established idiom, if followed, keeps the new record-save error-safe by default — but nothing enforces that convention on new code, so a new admin-record save function that echoes `name`/`phone`/`email`/`birthdate` into an Error message or console.error argument would be a first violation of this project's otherwise-consistent pattern.

findings.claim: (5) The roster page has a standing, reused generation/isCurrent co-guard (createRouteLoadMachine, src/lib/loading/routeLoad.ts) already used to prevent stale collective-switch writes on deactivate/reinstate/reorder/rename. A new record-editor save MUST capture `routeLoad.generation` AFTER triggering its own write (not at entry) and gate any state-writing continuation on `routeLoad.isCurrent(g)`, exactly like handleDeactivateConfirm/handleReinstate already do. Separately, the page's `reset({isSwitch})` callback explicitly nulls out per-row transient state (pendingDeactivateId/deactivateRefusal/deactivateActionError) ONLY on an actual collective switch (isSwitch===true), with an explicit code comment on why: 'a half-armed confirm or stale refusal is about a row the next tree may not even contain.' A newly-added open-editor state (e.g. an 'editingMemberId' plus its own pending/error flags) has NO existing reset-on-switch wiring and will need the identical treatment added to this callback, or a mid-flight collective switch will leave a record editor open/pending against a memberId belonging to the PREVIOUS collective's tree.

findings.claim: (5b) No cross-db bleed for the same person/member across two different collective(database) parents is directly enforced by ANY existing per-row keying today, because rosterData.ts's listActiveMembers is already scoped to ONE cfg/db per call (loadRoster(cfg) hits one entu db), and the page reloads rows wholesale on every collective switch (routeLoad.load). A record fetched by personId (not by (personId, dbEntityId) composite) risks resolving the WRONG collective's admin_member_record if the fetch layer ever queries by person alone instead of by (person, database-parent) — admin_member_record's own schema parents it under `database` with required cardinality 1, so the correct join key is the pair, not personId alone.

findings.claim: (8b) The contract specifies prefill via 'resolveField narrower-wins' for BOTH name and email. But resolveField's narrower-wins ordering explicitly prefers a PRIVATE-tier holder first (NARROWNESS: private=0 < domain=1 < public=2) — unlike rosterData.ts's own toRosterRow, which deliberately does NOT use resolveField for name specifically because narrower-wins 'would let a PRIVATE-only name leak through' onto the domain-shared roster row (documented rationale in rosterData.ts itself). The new admin_member_record.name field is schema'd as sharing:'domain' (visible to every member). If prefill copies resolveField's narrowest (possibly PRIVATE-tier) profile name into that domain-shared field, it promotes a value the person had ONLY shared privately into domain-wide visibility — the exact leak toRosterRow's own doc comment says resolveField must never be used for a name that becomes domain-visible. This is a genuine privacy-shape tension worth flagging to the PO/spec authors before implementation, not an existing code bug (no code implements this yet).
